MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #7 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a multiple of 9? (1 mark)
   A. 62
   B. 65
   C. 64
   D. 63

2. Which of these shows 305 in words? (1 mark)
   A. three hundred and five
   B. thirty-five
   C. four hundred and five
   D. three hundred and fifty

3. Round 553 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 500
   B. 550
   C. 540
   D. 560

4. A school has 1,845 pupils in the lower classes and 2,367 pupils in the upper classes. How many pupils are in the school? (1 mark)
   A. 4,212 pupils
   B. 4,312 pupils
   C. 3,102 pupils
   D. 4,202 pupils

5. Work out 3,568 + 2,276. (1 mark)
   A. 5,744
   B. 5,854
   C. 5,844
   D. 5,734

6. How many times do you need to regroup when you add 2,999 + 3,001? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 2
   C. 0
   D. 3

7. Work out 9,000 − 6,450. (1 mark)
   A. 2,450
   B. 2,550
   C. 3,450
   D. 2,560

8. Work out 6,120 − 3,845. (1 mark)
   A. 2,275
   B. 2,175
   C. 2,285
   D. 3,725

9. When multiplying 24 × 35, why do we write a zero in the ones place of the second partial product? (1 mark)
   A. To make the answer bigger
   B. Because 35 ends in 5
   C. Because we are multiplying by 30, which is 3 tens
   D. Because 24 ends in 4

10. Estimate 38 × 22 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 900
   B. 700
   C. 8,000
   D. 800

11. What is 25 × 100? (1 mark)
   A. 2,500
   B. 250
   C. 25,000
   D. 125

12. What is 83 ÷ 9? (1 mark)
   A. 9 remainder 2
   B. 10 remainder 2
   C. 9 remainder 3
   D. 8 remainder 11

13. To check 32 × 3 = 96 using division we work out (1 mark)
   A. 96 ÷ 3
   B. 96 ÷ 32 × 3
   C. 96 − 32
   D. 32 ÷ 3

14. What is 72 ÷ 6? (1 mark)
   A. 11
   B. 22
   C. 12
   D. 13

15. Change 19/4 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 5 3/4
   B. 4 4/4
   C. 3 4/4
   D. 4 3/4

16. Chebet writes another set of fractions. Which of these is a mixed fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 9/9
   B. 5/12
   C. 7/4
   D. 2 5/8

17. In the fraction 9/11, what does the numerator 9 tell us? (1 mark)
   A. The size of each part in centimetres
   B. How many of the equal parts are taken
   C. How many equal parts the whole has
   D. The number of wholes

18. Which is greater, 1.2 or 1.19? (1 mark)
   A. 1.19
   B. They are equal
   C. It cannot be told
   D. 1.2

19. A stick is 1.5 m long. How many centimetres is that? (1 mark)
   A. 1,500 cm
   B. 15 cm
   C. 150 cm
   D. 105 cm

20. What is the total value of the digit 6 in 5.68? (1 mark)
   A. 0.06
   B. 6
   C. 0.6
   D. 600

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Change 2 1/3 and 1 5/6 to improper fractions. (4 marks)

22. Divide 47 by 5. Check your answer using multiplication and addition. (3 marks)

23. Work out 12 × 21 showing both partial products. (3 marks)

24. Fill in the 3 times table from 3 × 1 to 3 × 10. Describe one pattern you notice. (4 marks)

25. A hundred square has 60 of its small squares shaded. Write the shaded part as a fraction and as a decimal. (2 marks)

26. Write 4,605 in words and 305 in words. Then say which is greater. (4 marks)

27. Divide 91 by 7 and check by multiplication. (3 marks)

28. A stadium seats 9,000 people. During a match 6,450 seats are taken. How many seats are empty? (3 marks)

29. Work out 48 × 21 and check the answer by estimating first. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #7 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — 63
   63 = 9 × 7, so 63 is a multiple of 9.

2. A — three hundred and five
   305 = three hundred and five. Say the hundreds, then "and", then the tens and ones.

3. B — 550
   Look at the ones digit 3. It is less than 5, so keep the tens digit. 553 rounds to 550.

4. A — 4,212 pupils
   Add 1,845 + 2,367 = 4,212 pupils.

5. C — 5,844
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 3,568 + 2,276 = 5,844.

6. D — 3
   Check each column from the right for a total of 10 or more, remembering the carried digit. 2,999 + 3,001 needs 3 regroupings.

7. B — 2,550
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 9,000 − 6,450 = 2,550. Check: 2,550 + 6,450 = 9,000.

8. A — 2,275
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 6,120 − 3,845 = 2,275. Check: 2,275 + 3,845 = 6,120.

9. C — Because we are multiplying by 30, which is 3 tens
   24 × 30 = 24 × 3 × 10 = 720, so the ones place holds a 0.

10. D — 800
   38 rounds to 40 and 22 rounds to 20. 40 × 20 = 800.

11. A — 2,500
   Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 25 × 100 = 2,500.

12. A — 9 remainder 2
   9 × 9 = 81 and 83 − 81 = 2. So 83 ÷ 9 = 9 remainder 2. Check: 9 × 9 + 2 = 83.

13. A — 96 ÷ 3
   Division undoes multiplication: 96 ÷ 3 = 32.

14. C — 12
   6 × 12 = 72, so 72 ÷ 6 = 12.

15. D — 4 3/4
   19 ÷ 4 = 4 remainder 3. The whole number is 4 and the fraction is 3/4, so 19/4 = 4 3/4.

16. D — 2 5/8
   A mixed fraction has a whole number and a proper fraction, like 2 5/8.

17. B — How many of the equal parts are taken
   The numerator is the top number. In 9/11 it says that 9 parts are taken.

18. D — 1.2
   Compare the tenths first. 1.2 is greater than 1.19.

19. C — 150 cm
   0.5 m = 50 cm, so 1.5 m = 100 cm + 50 cm = 150 cm.

20. C — 0.6
   The digit 6 is in the tenths place, so its total value is 0.6.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: 7/3 and 11/6
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for 2 × 3 + 1 = 7 so 7/3; 2 marks for 1 × 6 + 5 = 11 so 11/6.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: 9 remainder 2. Check: 9 × 5 + 2 = 47.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 9, 1 mark for remainder 2, 1 mark for the check.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: 252
   Working / marking points: 12 × 1 = 12 (1 mark); 12 × 20 = 240 (1 mark); 12 + 240 = 252 (1 mark).

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30. Each product is 3 more than the one before it (or the products alternate odd and even).
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the table (1 mark if one or two errors), 2 marks for a correct pattern with a reason.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: 60/100 and 0.6 (or 0.60)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the fraction and 1 mark for the decimal.

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: 4,605 is four thousand, six hundred and five. 305 is three hundred and five. 4,605 is greater.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct wording and 1 mark each for the comparison and its reason (more digits).

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: 13. Check: 13 × 7 = 91.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 7 × 13, 1 mark for 13, 1 mark for the check.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2,550 seats
   Working / marking points: 9,000 − 6,450 with regrouping across zeros. 1 mark for the setup, 1 mark for regrouping, 1 mark for the answer with units.

29. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate 50 × 20 = 1,000. Exact: 48 × 1 = 48 and 48 × 20 = 960, so 1,008.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the estimate, 1 mark for each partial product and 1 mark for the sum 1,008.
